sections.heading: Roof Deck Repair and Replacement, Defined

c.v: The roof deck

runs.v: is the plywood or OSB sheathing that spans the rafters, the structural substrate that anchors every roofing nail and carries the underlayment and the covering. Roof deck repair and replacement removes rotted, delaminated, or sagging sheathing and re-decks the roof.

The roof decking is the part of a roofing system nobody sees until it fails: shingles, underlayment, and flashing all depend on a wood deck that can hold a nail. Anyone searching for roof deck repair and replacement Newark NJ usually has a soft spot underfoot, a sag between the rafters, or a contractor who found rot at tear-off, and needs two answers: how much of the deck has to come out, and what caused the rot. On a rooftop deck, a walkable deck built over a flat roof, the same sheathing sits under the waterproofing, and waterproofing and flashing are essential there too.

sections.heading: What Should I Do If My Roof Decking Is Rotted?

c.v: Stop the water, stay off the soft area, find the cause, and replace every rotted panel before a new covering goes on; rotted roof decking is never roofed over.

runs.v: A structural inspection is crucial before any roof repair or replacement, and the safe way to judge rot is from the attic and from sound decking, because a foot can go through a rotted panel. Repair planning starts with how far the rot runs, what let the water in, and whether the rafters under it are sound.
Emergency Tarping After Storm Damage and Heavy Rain

If water is coming in now, emergency tarping comes first. Newark Quality Roofing answers an active roof leak 24/7 and targets a 1–4 hour emergency response, and a tarp stops active water entry until the permanent repair, because emergency repairs prevent further damage: every day of heavy rain on an open roof soaks more decking, wet insulation, and drywall and adds interior damage. Newark roofs face frequent storm damage from nor'easters; falling branches and wind damage are the usual causes of a punctured deck, and storm damage repairs then restore every component the storm damaged, from the sheathing up. Emergency roof repair services end with a written estimate for the permanent work.
Find the Roof Leak Before Replacing the Decking

Decking rots from the top when water gets past the roof covering and from below when the attic traps moisture, so a re-deck that skips the cause rots again. Roughly 90–95% of roof leaks originate at flashing details, an industry estimate attributed to the NRCA, and a failed flashing, a gutter overflowing at the eave, or wind-driven rain at a wall joint is the usual source, so the fix can include valley repairs or an exterior repair at the wall as well as the deck. Humidity and freeze-thaw cycles accelerate wood rot in roof decking: Newark roofs go through dozens of freeze-thaw cycles each winter, commonly estimated at 30–50, and ice dams frequently form on Newark roofs, pushing meltwater under the shingles at the eaves. Proper attic ventilation helps prevent ice dam formation by keeping the deck cold, working alongside insulation and air sealing.

sections.heading: Deck Repair or Full Roof Replacement? What Newark Homeowners Should Know

c.v: Repair the deck in sections when the rot stays local; plan a full roof replacement when the covering is at the end of its life or the damage is widespread.

runs.v: Contractor-consensus thresholds set the line: replace the roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, and granule loss exceeding 30% indicates a roof beyond repair.

Widespread damage to the roof covering does not mean the whole roof deck has to be replaced. The deck is replaced where it is rotted, delaminated, or water-soaked, and sound sheathing stays, so a quote that assumes a full re-deck because 25% of the roof is damaged is mixing up the covering with the decking under it. Inspecting for water staining and deterioration is necessary during roof replacement, which is why tear-off is where most hidden rot on the existing roof is found.
Roofing Materials, Weight, and the Deck

Roofing materials load the deck differently. Asphalt shingles are the lightest common covering, metal roofs offer superior durability and last longer than asphalt, tile roofs can last over 50 years with proper care, and slate roofs are known for their lifetime durability, but replacing heavy roofing materials, or switching to one, requires a structural analysis of the rafters and roof deck. Heavy snow loads in northern New Jersey require roofs to be structurally sound, the climate in Newark calls for roofs strong enough to endure coastal storms and heavy snows, and dark roof surfaces can exceed 160°F on a summer afternoon, so the deck cycles through heat and cold all year; ensuring structural integrity starts with the deck.
Re-Decking During a New Roof Installation

A new roof installation is the one time the whole deck is exposed, so a good written estimate for a full roof replacement names a per-sheet price for hidden rot before work begins, and the existing roof covering comes off down to the wood. Rotted panels are replaced one by one, sagging sections are re-supported, and the new underlayment and ice barrier go down on a deck that can hold every nail.
Flat Roof and Rooftop Deck Waterproofing

On a flat roof, the decking stays dry only as long as the membrane, flashing, and drains above it do. Waterproofing and flashing are essential for flat roofs and rooftop decks, where a walkable deck sits over the roof membrane and hides the drains and seams beneath it.

sections.heading: Do I Need a Permit to Replace My Roof in New Jersey?

c.v: Not for the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home: detached one- and two-family roof repairs and roof-covering replacement are ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, with no permit, inspection, or notice to the construction official.

runs.v: Other buildings need a permit once repairs exceed 25% of the roof area in 12 months.

Structural changes to the roof decking or framing, such as replacing or reinforcing rafters, require a construction permit under New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code, and in Newark the city's construction code office administers roofing permits under that code. Contractors must hold a valid New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor registration, and the registered contractor should secure any permit the structural work needs before work begins; navigating roof deck repair in Newark means balancing structural engineering and local building codes. Newark's historic preservation rules require review for visible exterior work: properties in the city's designated historic districts, Forest Hill among them, can need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Newark Landmarks and Historic Preservation Commission before changes that alter the roof's appearance.

sections.heading: Roof Deck Repair and Replacement FAQs

faqs.q: What is the roof deck and why does it need replacing?

runs.v: The roof deck is the plywood or OSB sheathing that spans the rafters and anchors every roofing nail under the underlayment and the covering. It needs replacing when trapped moisture decays the sheathing until it can no longer hold a fastener and the roof loses wind resistance, per InterNACHI, because roofing nails penetrate at least 3/4 inch into solid deck, per ARMA.

faqs.q: How thick should roof sheathing be for the rafter spacing?

runs.v: Roof sheathing carries an APA span rating that sets the maximum rafter spacing: 7/16-inch panels rate 24/16, 15/32-inch panels 32/16, 19/32-inch panels 40/20, and 23/32-inch panels 48/24, per APA – The Engineered Wood Association. InterNACHI cites a 5/8-inch minimum at 24-inch rafter spacing, and panels thinner than 1/2 inch over rafters spaced more than 20 inches on center take H-clips or blocking, per IRC Section R803.2.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace your roof?

runs.v: Replace the deck section when the sheathing is rotted, delaminated, swollen, or sagging, and replace the roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost; repair when the decay stays localized. The 25–30% area rule and the 50% cost rule are contractor-consensus thresholds.

faqs.q: Can you reroof over a rotted or water-soaked deck?

runs.v: No. The IRC reroofing provisions in Section R908 prohibit roofing over a water-soaked or deteriorated deck, so the rotted sheathing comes off before the new covering goes on, and sheathing that cannot grip a nail leaves the covering prone to wind uplift, per InterNACHI.

faqs.q: Does swollen OSB dry out, or does it have to be replaced?

runs.v: Swollen OSB swells at the edges and delaminates irreversibly once saturated, so saturated OSB gets replaced rather than dried out, while plywood dries more uniformly and partly recovers, per InterNACHI and trade guidance. A Newark Quality Roofing inspection separates plywood that recovers from panels past recovery before a re-deck quote.

A hidden-rot re-deck added during a re-roof runs about $50–$120 per 4-by-8 sheet, per contractor cost data, and Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: Is OSB or plywood better for a roof deck?

runs.v: OSB costs less than plywood per sheet, while plywood dries more uniformly and partly recovers after wetting, whereas OSB swells at the edges and delaminates irreversibly once saturated, per InterNACHI and trade guidance. Both carry an APA span rating that sets the maximum rafter spacing, and either grips a roofing nail at least 3/4 inch deep, per ARMA.

faqs.q: What does a roof inspection check on the deck?
